title: Guard Retention Layers
shortDefinition: Guard retention has 7 layers: distance → feet → knees → frames → hips → shoulders → re-attack. Each layer lost drops you to the next.
whyItMatters: If you rely on one layer, the passer kills it and flattens you. Retention layers tell you exactly what to do as you get passed step by step.
deepExplanation:
7 retention layers, outside to inside:

1. Distance, feet threaten, hands fight. When the passer gets close, you have lost this layer.
2. Feet, sole-to-hip, sole-to-bicep. Push their hips away, break passing rhythm.
3. Knees, knee pummel, shin-to-shin, knee shield. Block chest-to-chest, create wedges.
4. Frames, forearm frame, elbow frame. Maintain space when knees get cleared.
5. Hips, hip escape, shrimp, whizzer. Turn hips off the pass line when upper structure breaks.
6. Shoulders, granby roll, shoulder-in, back exposure escape. When hips can no longer turn.
7. Re-attack, wrestle-up, leg pummel, turtle with underhook. Final layer, switch defense to offense.

Retention is not linear 1→7. Good retention jumps layers based on the passer’s intent: if they commit to bodylock, skip distance/feet and go straight to knees + frames. If they back step, reopen distance with technical stand-up.
beginnerView:
7 layers with 3 recurring questions:
1. Can your feet still threaten? → Feet/knees
2. Can you still keep a wedge (knee)? → Knees/frames
3. Can your hips still turn? → Hips/shoulders

When flattened, do not keep trying to reguard, switch to re-attack (wrestle-up or turtle). Golden rule: never let their chest touch your chest at any layer.
advancedView: Advanced retention does not just keep Guard, it baits the passer into traps. Leave a gap in the distance layer so they commit to a pass line, then hit a sweep or wrestle-up. Use non-linear layering: if they are used to bodylocking past your knee shield, drop the knee shield early and switch to shin-to-shin + off-balance. Every layer is a counter opportunity: feet layer threatens sweeps, knees layer threatens wrestle-up or triangle, frames layer threatens back takes if they overcommit. Great retention plays at high layers (distance/knees) but is ready to drop to re-attack when they get low.
